documents_checked.text:
Academic Misconduct means conduct by a Student, other than conduct constituting Academic
Record Fraud or General Misconduct, that is dishonest or unfair in connection with any academic
work, such as:

(b) in relation to the preparation or presentation of any assessed item of work; or
(c) in relation to the conduct of research or any other similar academic activity.

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Verified authority for standing account actions, protected student identity and meaningful assessment oversight.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N005 (Sept 2026) supersedes N153 and delegates operational ICT account/credential rules to the 'Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Appropriate Use Procedures' (vp 218 L011), which is unavailable in the bundle and could either prohibit/verify standing account delegation (No) or leave it unaddressed (Yes).
case_summary.case_note: Curtin restricts ICT assets to authorised purposes (N005), requires human oversight for AI (N001), mandates student-authored assessment verified by authenticity checks (N002), and prohibits impersonation and unfair academic conduct (N136, N141). Critical gap is Uncertain because N005 (effective August/September 2026) superseded N153 and moved operational account-use rules to the unavailable ICT Appropriate Use Procedures. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review on 2026-11-15.

15. Right of appeal
15.1 A Student may appeal a decision of the Authorised Oﬃcer or Student Conduct Panel that Student
Misconduct has occurred and/or any Penalty imposed:
(a) within 7 days of a decision made or Penalty imposed under the Pathway 1 Process; or
(b) within 14 days of a decision made or Penalty imposed under the Pathway 2 Process.
15.2 In exceptional circumstances, the Academic Registrar may give a Student more time to appeal.
